AuthService mixes unrelated concerns: login throttling, user administration (findAll/update/countByCondition), avatar file deletion, password reset, 2FA setup, Set-Cookie string building, and refresh-token/dashboard pass-through methods.
JwtAuthGuard.handleRequest holds the same token-expiry and unauthorized mapping that is copied in JwtTwoFactorGuard, so the invariant is defined in two places.

JwtTwoFactorGuard.handleRequest and canActivate copy JwtAuthGuard: the TokenExpiredError -> ForbiddenException('tokenExpired', StatusCodesList.TokenExpired) mapping and the err/!user -> UnauthorizedException rule. This auth-failure policy should live in one shared base class or factory that takes the strategy name.
transformError builds an untyped validation-error array whose shape the exception filter must copy. The contract is defined implicitly instead of in one shared abstraction.

I18nExceptionFilterPipe is an ExceptionFilter (@Catch(HttpException)) that translates messages, logs and writes the HTTP response. This concern is unrelated to the validation pipes in this module. It is misnamed as a pipe and belongs with the filters.
getCookieForLogOut() and buildResponsePayload() build HTTP Set-Cookie header strings (HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure, Max-Age). That is presentation/transport logic, not an application concern.

login() checks passwords with user.validatePassword, enforces the ACTIVE-status login rule, and returns ExceptionTitleList/StatusCodesList error tuples. This is authentication business logic for the application layer (e.g. AuthService), not persistence.

CustomBaseEntity extends TypeORM BaseEntity, so it inherits database methods like save, remove and find. Its id, createdAt and updatedAt fields carry ORM column mapping (PrimaryGeneratedColumn, CreateDateColumn, UpdateDateColumn with 'timestamp' types, SQL CURRENT_TIMESTAMP defaults and onUpdate). This is persistence logic for the infrastructure layer, but the file is declared domain.

EmailTemplateEntity carries persistence responsibilities that belong to the infrastructure layer: @Entity({ name: 'email_templates' }) maps it to a table, @Column() decorators map its fields, and @Index({ unique: true }) on title defines a database constraint. These sit in a file declared as domain.

Class `RefreshToken` extends TypeORM `BaseEntity`, which makes it an Active Record object with save/remove/find persistence methods. This persistence responsibility belongs to the infrastructure layer, not the domain layer.

RoleEntity carries persistence-mapping responsibilities that belong to the infrastructure layer: @Entity({ name: 'role' }) sets the table name, @Column('varchar', { length: 100 }) and @Column('text') set column types, @Index and @Unique set constraints, and @JoinTable sets the 'role_permission' join table with 'roleId' and 'permissionId' columns. These responsibilities sit in a domain-layer file.
